items.title: Published 1.8.1 exact runtime pins prevent current Click patch and markdown-it-py releases
items.body:
The current PyPI metadata for `scriv==1.8.1` declares exact runtime pins, including `click==8.5.0` and `markdown-it-py==4.2.0`. PyPI now serves Click 8.5.1 and markdown-it-py 4.3.0. This prevents a consuming project's universal lock from taking even the newer Click patch release.

Minimal reproduction (resolution only; installs nothing):

```sh
python -m pip install --dry-run scriv==1.8.1 click==8.5.1
python -m pip install --dry-run scriv==1.8.1 markdown-it-py==4.3.0
```

Both constraints conflict with Scriv's exact requirements. The same limits remain after `uv lock --upgrade`. The metadata is available at https://pypi.org/pypi/scriv/1.8.1/json .

Could the published library requirements use tested compatible ranges for its direct dependencies, keeping exact application/development resolutions in Scriv's own lock? For example, after validating the current APIs, `click>=8.5,<9` and `markdown-it-py>=4.2,<5` would permit these releases without consumers overriding Scriv's declared contract. The exact complete transitive list in `Requires-Dist` also merits checking against the project's intended direct runtime dependencies.

Our workaround preserves the published constraints and explicitly records both older versions as upstream-constrained in the dependency inventory; it does not bypass the resolver or hide conflicts. We are updating the full dependency tree in https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/pull/152 and will refresh the universal lock when compatible metadata is released.

items.title: Relax exact runtime dependency pins to allow compatible downstream updates
items.body:
Scriv 1.8.1 pins all twelve runtime dependencies with `==`. This prevents consumers from resolving even compatible patch updates. PyPI currently provides click 8.5.1 and markdown-it-py 4.3.0, while Scriv requires click 8.5.0 and markdown-it-py 4.2.0.

Minimal reproduction (uv 0.13.8, Python 3.15):

```sh
uv pip install --dry-run --python python3.15 'scriv==1.8.1' 'click==8.5.1'
```

Resolution fails because both exact click versions cannot be selected. The same conflict occurs with `markdown-it-py==4.3.0`.

In link-foundation/links-notation#406 we retain Scriv's required versions in native uv and hashed pip locks, rather than ignoring its metadata or forcing an untested override. The rest of the tooling resolves current releases and passes pip-audit.

Could Scriv use compatible requirements in its published library metadata (for example `click>=8.5.0,<9` and `markdown-it-py>=4.2.0,<5`) and keep exact development resolution in its own lockfile? That would preserve reproducibility for Scriv's development environment while allowing downstream applications to adopt compatible fixes. Tests against the lower bounds and current releases would validate those ranges.

items.title: Test fail with click 8.2.0
items.body:
Hi,

click 8.2.0 [(changes)](https://github.com/pallets/click/blob/main/CHANGES.rst) entered in Debian and I observed a test failure:
```shell
========================================================================= FAILURES ==========================================================================
________________________________________________________________________ test_dashm _________________________________________________________________________

    def test_dashm():
        ok, output = run_command([sys.executable, "-m", "scriv"])
        print(output)
>       assert ok
E       assert False

tests/test_process.py:12: AssertionError
------------------------------------------------------------------- Captured stdout call --------------------------------------------------------------------
Usage: scriv [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  Manage changelogs.

  Version 1.5.1

Options:
  --version  Show the version and exit.
  --help     Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  collect         Collect and combine fragments into the changelog.
  create          Create a new changelog fragment.
  github-release  Create GitHub releases from the changelog.
```
Root cause is that executing _scriv_ without parameters on the shell returns an error code = 2 and the output is redirected to _stderr_ instead of _stdout_.
Changing:
```python
ok, output = run_command([sys.executable, "-m", "scriv"])
```
to:
```python
ok, output = run_command([sys.executable, "-m", "scriv", "--help"])
```
fixes the issue.

System info:
- Debian Sid
- Python 3.13
- click 8.2.0
- scriv 1.5.1

Thanks for maintaining this program.

Kind Regards
